title: Can airport scanners see you naked?
description:
Shoes on or off? Laptops in or out? And don’t get us started on the rules around liquids! Getting through airport security never seems to be simple. It’s there for a reason, of course. But there are so many rules and why do they seem to be different everywhere you go?

We’re joined by science journalist and presenter Caroline Steel to talk about everything from the miles long luggage belts our suitcases travel on, how x-ray scanners work, what they’re looking for and whether or not they can ACTUALLY see us naked.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討機場安檢技術的運作原理與各項規則背後的原因。主持人 Hannah Gelbart 與科學記者 Caroline Steel 深入解析託運行李在廣大地下輸送帶上的安檢程序、毫米波人體掃描儀如何穿透衣服偵測隱蔽物品，以及安檢人員為何不會看到乘客的裸體影像。節目亦介紹最新 CT 掃描器如何透過 X 光打造 3D 彩色影像來辨識物品、2006 年液體炸藥陰謀引發的 100 ml 液體限制由來，以及離子移動光譜儀能在數秒內偵測出十億分之一克的化學痕跡。最後，她們討論了入境時的海關與生物安全檢查，並展望未來的步行掃描與臉部辨識通關技術。
summaryEn: This episode of What in the World explores the science and technology behind airport security rules and equipment. Host Hannah Gelbart and science journalist Caroline Steel explain how checked baggage travels through massive underground belt systems, how millimetre wave body scanners detect hidden objects without showing nude images to security staff, and how modern CT scanners produce 3D color-coded X-ray images of hand luggage. They also discuss the origin of liquid restrictions following a foiled 2006 plot, how swab machines can detect chemical traces down to a billionth of a gram, the purpose of customs and biosecurity checks on arrival, and future developments like walk-through scanners and facial recognition corridors.
